reason: The tester deferred Cursor testing after the Claude rerun, while Q06-c requires both providers. The first attempt sent no follow-up before release; in the Claude rerun, browser Enter time bounds overlap the T+9 status sample, so strict sample-before-follow-up ordering and exact turn-completion-to-release timing are not proven. These are test-coverage limits, not established product failures.
observations: The running QA Relay used the unchanged 10m idle_release_timeout for both pools. In the first attempt, both workspaces stayed running through 00:32:50 UTC, then exited with done 0 and were deleted around 00:33 to 00:34 UTC. No follow-up was sent before release because the per-provider completion mapping was not established in time; this attempt cannot test timer reset.

For the Claude rerun, the tester confirmed the selected self-hosted Claude environment maps to QA pool qa-claude. One benign turn in a new QA workspace completed visibly by 00:50:01.6 UTC. The same browser conversation received one follow-up with marker QA-Q06-CLAUDE-FOLLOWUP-R2-EF6DF596 and returned a normal reply without a new workspace or runner-wait banner.

The control-plane sample at 00:59:02 UTC showed that same Claude workspace running, but the browser follow-up Enter occurred somewhere between 00:59:00.5 and 00:59:07.5 UTC, so the sample's ordering relative to Enter is unknown. The workspace stayed up beyond the original idle window and until at least 01:09:03 UTC; Relay queued clean-exit deletion at 01:09:33 UTC and the workspace was gone by 01:10:04 UTC. The exact worker release time precedes the reaper sweep and was not observed.

The Claude browser subsequently showed the same session paused and ready to resume on a different runner. No Cursor rerun prompt was sent because the tester requested Claude-only QA. All QA workspaces are gone, no fault or manual shutdown was applied, and both baseline pools remain healthy.
